scope: Official New York City Council and New York State legislative records for Commercial Rent Stabilization, including complete recovered Council testimony, active Albany bill records and sponsor memoranda, official pro-bill public statements, and timestamp-bound transcripts of supportive public-event speeches.

legislation.summary: Proposed a commercial-rent registration and regulation system for covered retail, manufacturing, professional, service, and office spaces, administered through a Commercial Rent Guidelines Board.
Reintroduced the proposed municipal commercial-rent registration and regulation system with a nine-member Commercial Rent Guidelines Board.

Calls on New York State to pass A.5568A/S.8319, the New York City Small Business Rent Stabilization Act. This is a resolution in the current state-legislation lineage, not a municipal commercial-rent-stabilization bill.

coverage_notes: Council Member Stephen T. Levin is the only public official in this hearing classified here as directly supporting Intro 1796.
Council Member Kalman Yeger argued against Intro 1796 and is not included in this supportive-statement collection; the official transcript remains the canonical record of his opposition.
Council Member Mark Treyger's substantive statement concerned Intro 568, not commercial rent, and is not included.
The Small Business Services commissioner and deputy commissioners testified for the administration but did not endorse Intro 1796; their testimony remains in the official transcript.
Public-official records are selected by complete transcript turn, not sentence fragments. Scope notes prevent related-measure support or problem recognition from being promoted into bill endorsement.

official_state_statements.title: Senator Salazar and Assembly Member Gallagher introduce the Small Business Survival Act
official_state_statements.source_kind: official New York State Senate press release
official_state_statements.scope_note: The complete attributed pro-bill quotations are retained. These are published statements, not represented as chamber-floor transcripts.

records.name: Julia Salazar
records.role_at_statement: New York State Senator and S8319 prime sponsor
records.text: The Small Business Survival Act would be a lifeline for small businesses in New York City by capping outrageous rent hikes and guaranteeing lease renewals. Corporate landlords are charging rents so high that the only business owners who can afford to pay are corporate chains. Or, they’re keeping storefronts vacant until larger, wealthier tenants come along. This is a toxic and now commonplace pattern that is shuttering our local businesses, putting New Yorkers out of work, and turning our vibrant neighborhoods into chain malls.

records.name: Emily Gallagher
records.role_at_statement: New York State Assembly Member and A5568A prime sponsor
records.text: Small businesses are what make New York special, but they are increasingly being pushed out by greedy corporate actors. In the 20 years I’ve been in my neighborhood, I’ve seen so many beloved businesses close because of unaffordable rents or because big landlords would rather wait for a corporate chain to come along. With the Small Business Survival Act, we will cap rent, guarantee leases, and ensure our community businesses are actually owned by the members of our community.

records.name: Olympia Kazi
records.text: I want to thank State Senator Julia Salazar and Assembly Member Emily Gallagher for introducing this critical legislation to enact a common-sense, fundamental protection for commercial tenants. For more than half a century, communities have fought to defend beloved small businesses, nonprofits, and cultural institutions from displacement and erasure. With renewed leadership in New York State and New York City that centers affordability and justice, I am hopeful—and confident—that the moment to pass commercial rent stabilization has arrived.

records.name: Small Business United
records.text: Small businesses are struggling to survive in New York City because they cannot keep up with continuously rising costs, including the rising cost of rent. This crisis is the result of treating commercial space as a commodity to make corporate real estate companies richer, rather than as community infrastructure to support our neighborhoods. New York must pass the Small Business Survival Act before our local business owners are forced to close their doors and seek opportunities elsewhere.

official_state_statements.title: Senator Salazar rallies for Jimmy's Corner and Small Business Rent Stabilization
official_state_statements.source_kind: official New York State Senate press release
official_state_statements.scope_note: The complete attributed pro-bill quotations in the official release are retained. They supplement, but do not replace, the event transcript.

records.name: Julia Salazar
records.role_at_statement: New York State Senator and S8319 prime sponsor
records.text: Jimmy’s Corner is a beloved small business and member of the community. It has had an impact that corporate businesses could never replicate. Unfortunately, there are countless small businesses just like Jimmy’s that are being squeezed out of our city. Big landlords are charging rents so high that the only business owners who can afford to pay are corporate chains. Or, they’re keeping storefronts vacant until larger, wealthier tenants come along. This is a toxic and now commonplace pattern that is shuttering our small businesses, putting New Yorkers out of work, and turning our vibrant neighborhoods into chain malls. Small Business Rent Stabilization would be a lifeline for local businesses in New York City by capping outrageous rent hikes, guaranteeing lease renewals, and protecting at-will tenants.

records.name: Emily Gallagher
records.role_at_statement: New York State Assembly Member and A5568A prime sponsor
records.text: Small, local businesses make our neighborhoods vibrant, our communities safer, and our city unique. But increasingly, you have to be a huge chain or a venture-backed business to make it in this city. Landlords leave storefronts vacant while they wait for these cookie cutter establishments to come in and price out beloved local counterparts. The Small Business Rent Stabilization Act will protect our local businesses and ensure NYC continues to be a place where they can thrive.

records.name: Olympia Kazi
records.role_at_statement: NYC Artist Coalition and Music Workers Alliance co-founder
records.text: What is happening with Jimmy's Corner—recently described by a patron as “the only real bar in the neighborhood”—perfectly illustrates how unfairly tilted the scales are for small businesses right now. Our government has left New York City’s commercial tenants largely unprotected. Current policies fail to recognize that these establishments provide essential services, create jobs, and contribute deep social and cultural value—often for decades. In this case, that legacy spans 54 years. Yet all of that can be erased overnight, and even leveraged for profit by landlords. The story of Jimmy’s Corner is a wake-up call. It underscores the urgent need for the city to finally establish meaningful protections for commercial tenants and we need to start with the most fundamental of them all, the passage of commercial rent stabilization.

records.name: Linda B. Rosenthal
records.role_at_statement: New York State Assembly Member and Chair of the Assembly Committee on Housing
records.text: Jimmy's Corner is a New York institution, but could soon be forced to close its doors as a result of a dubious eviction proceeding. Nearly half of New York State's workforce is employed by small businesses, but drastic rent hikes and corporate greed have pushed thousands of these businesses to close in recent years. We need to act to lend a hand to New York City's beleaguered businesses by supporting Assemblymember Gallagher's legislation, the Small Business Rent Stabilization Act, which will protect at-will tenants, prohibit unaffordable rent hikes and guarantee lease renewals for small businesses across our city.

records.name: Jo Anne Simon
records.role_at_statement: New York State Assembly Member and A5568A co-sponsor
records.text: Local businesses are the backbone of New York City, but far too many are being forced out by skyrocketing commercial rents and price-gouging. Small-business rent stabilization will help protect the very neighborhood institutions that create jobs, build community, and give NYC its quintessential character. I am proud to support this effort and thank Assemblymember Gallagher and Senator Salazar for sponsoring this important legislation.

coverage_notes: No official chamber video or transcript was recovered for an A5568A or S8319 introduction or floor speech. Both bills remain in committee as of 2026-07-28.
Official sponsor memoranda and official press-release quotations are written public statements; public-event records are transcript-derived speeches.
The collection is additive, not a claim of exhaustive statewide public support. New source leads should enter through the same hash-bound, role-at-the-time, source-type-aware process.
